act-darpa.value: DARPA initiated AI Next / generative-AI programs from 2018 onward; by 2024-2026 expanding investment in AI safety and autonomous systems — continuing role as frontier-research patron beyond the Internet lineage

DoD declared TCP/IP its official standard March 1982; set January 1 1983 as mandatory cutover deadline. From RFC 675 (December 1974) to DoD mandate (March 1982): ~7.5 year lag to institutional mandate.

source.title: J. C. R. Licklider — Wikipedia (IPTO founding context)

child-internet.value: ICANN transition to global multistakeholder governance (October 1, 2016): US government ended oversight of IANA functions, transferring to international community

fe-cyclades-defund.value: French PTT (DGT) cut CYCLADES funding c.1978; network offline 1981. PTT invoked state monopoly on data transmission to block government funding of a competitor to Transpac.

fe-defense-funding.value: DARPA RFP for ARPANET: BBN awarded IMP contract January 1969; first IMP delivered August 30 1969 — approximately 3 years from Taylor's 1966 funding to first deployed node.

fe-gosip-osi-mandate.value: GOSIP 1988-1990 mandate suppressed TCP/IP federal procurement for ~5 years despite TCP/IP being operational since 1983. The mandate was largely toothless: lack of OSI products encouraged TCP/IP purchase anyway.

source.title: Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile — Wikipedia

fe-gosip-osi-mandate.value: GOSIP v1 published August 1988; FIPS 146-1 adopted February 15 1989; enforcement began August 15 1990 requiring OSI compliance for federal procurement. US National Research Council 1985 recommended migrating FROM TCP/IP TO OSI.

source.title: Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile — Wikipedia

fe-sputnik.value: Sputnik launched October 4 1957; ARPA created February 1958 — 4-month lag from crisis trigger to institutional response; ARPANET first deployed 1969 — 11-year cascade from Sputnik to operational packet network.

h-cloud-mobile.value: 2025: ~570 active submarine cable systems, ~80 under construction, spanning ~1.4-1.5 million km of seabed. Internet traffic terminating at 1,636 landing points worldwide (up from 1,444 in 2023). Physical substrate growth metric.

source.title: Enhancing Resilience of Submarine Internet Infrastructure — Internet Society

h-governance.value: January 2 2025: US Sixth Circuit Court vacated FCC 2024 net neutrality rules, ruling FCC lacked authority to reclassify ISPs under Title II (post-Loper Bright Chevron-deference reversal).

source.title: US appeals court overturns FCC net neutrality rules — JURIST
Paul Baran, RAND, On Distributed Communications Vol. I — National Security Archive

pf-baran.value: 1965: RAND recommended Air Force build distributed network; project assigned to Defense Communications Agency whose staff lacked digital expertise; Baran recommended shelving it. AT&T told Baran 'it can't work, and if it did work, we don't want it'.

source.title: Paul Baran 1959-1965 — History of Computer Communications

value.basis: Historians and the US National Inventors Hall of Fame credit Baran AND Davies independently as co-inventors of packet switching, with Kleinrock credited for queueing theory analysis (not the switching concept itself). The contested Kleinrock claim is recorded at much lower weight.

Cerf and Kahn are the named co-authors of the 1974 TCP/IP paper and jointly received the Turing Award 2004. Pouzin/CYCLADES acknowledged in the paper for the datagram and end-host reliability model; Gerard Le Lann carried CYCLADES concepts into TCP.

proposed:icann.value: December 5 2024: Kurt Erik Lindqvist became new president and CEO of ICANN (previously CEO of London Internet Exchange since 2019).

disputed_alternatives.value_found: 1990 (year confirmed; February 28 exact date not corroborated by independent source)

second_source.title: A Brief History of the Internet — Internet Society

rel-x25.value: X.25 public data networks achieved 'large global coverage during the 1980s and into the 1990s'. Examples: TRANSPAC (France), DATAPAC (Canada), Telenet and Tymnet (USA). BT X.25 service persisted to 2019.

sw-arpanet.value: First ARPANET message sent October 29 1969 at 10:30 p.m. from UCLA to SRI: attempted 'login', only 'lo' transmitted before crash. First four-node ARPANET operational December 5, 1969.

source.title: The First Message Transmission — ICANN Blog

sw-cerf-kahn.value: 7 months: Cerf-Kahn paper May 1974 -> RFC 675 December 1974

sw-flag-day.value: ~9 years from Cerf-Kahn paper (May 1974) to operational flag day (January 1 1983); ~4 years from RFC 675 (December 1974) to TCP/IP v4 split (1978); ~5 years from split to flag day
